command -v pdftoppm

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
p.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages,1):
    text=page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    (p/f'page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(text)
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i} ===\\n{page.extract_text(extraction_mode=\"layout\")}' for i,page in enumerate(r.pages,1)))
print((p/'manuscript.txt').read_text()[:23000])
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
for i in range(1,18):
    for extension in ('txt','png'):
        (p/f'page-{i:02d}.{extension}').unlink(missing_ok=True)
(p/'manuscript.txt').unlink(missing_ok=True)
print('Removed temporary extraction and rendering files.')
PY"

strengths: MaskSub provides a simple, technically coherent training method: shared-weight masked predictions learn from detached unmasked predictions alongside supervised learning. It adds no inference-time branch and integrates into established training recipes. Its practical contribution and supporting evidence favor acceptance.

Improvements over strong baselines are consistent across model sizes. Table 1 reports gains of 0.6–0.7 percentage points at 400 epochs and 0.3–0.5 points at 800 epochs. Table A.12 reports ViT-B improving from 83.46±0.04 to 84.08±0.02, supporting the reliability of a central result.

The evaluation meaningfully accounts for additional computation. Table 7 compares 400-epoch MaskSub ViT-B against a 600-epoch baseline: 84.1% versus 83.7% at 25 versus 26 GPU-days. Table 8 also demonstrates a favorable accuracy–cost tradeoff against CoSub under the evaluated recipe.

Evidence extends beyond ImageNet classification to different architectures, pretrained-model fine-tuning, downstream vision tasks, and distribution shifts. Tables A.2–A.4 include segmentation and detection improvements; ImageNet-A accuracy increases from 36.8% to 41.9% for ViT-B. These results strengthen the contribution's usefulness.

The supplement supplies valuable ablations and reproduction details. Table A.6 supports the distillation component, Tables A.7–A.8 examine masking ratios and loss weights, and several experiments include three-run statistics. Algorithm 1, architecture-specific masking descriptions, detailed recipe tables, and a code link make implementation reasonably accessible.
weaknesses: Conceptual novelty is incremental relative to masked distillation and sub-model self-distillation, including the cited MaskedKD and CoSub. Table A.7 also shows that zero-mask self-distillation already improves accuracy from 77.4% to 78.4%, versus 79.2% with 50% masking. The evidence establishes a useful combination more convincingly than a fundamentally new learning mechanism.

The explanation of 'automatic difficulty control' exceeds the demonstrated evidence. Figure 3 shows epoch-averaged gradient norms, but does not establish that masked supervision is restricted to correctly learned examples. Every example receives the masked loss, including confidently incorrect predictions. Moreover, stop-gradient blocks differentiation through the target; shared parameters still allow masked-branch updates to change the main predictor. These qualifications affect the interpretation, rather than invalidating the algorithm.

Some comparative claims are insufficiently controlled. Table 6 combines competitors trained with weaker recipes with MaskSub using RSB, so it cannot isolate superiority of the distillation method or establish competitors' incompatibility with modern recipes. The controlled comparisons in Tables 8–9 are stronger evidence and warrant narrower claims.

Benefits depend on the setting and evaluation protocol. With the same MaskSub-pretrained ViT-B, adding MaskSub during CIFAR-100 fine-tuning reduces accuracy from 91.9% to 89.6% (Table 10). Section 4.2 states that CLIP fine-tuning improves final-epoch accuracy but leaves best-checkpoint performance unchanged. Furthermore, the 0.1-point BEiT-v2 improvements and small detection gains lack corresponding run-to-run uncertainty estimates, despite useful repeated experiments elsewhere.

Minor reporting errors need correction but do not determine the recommendation. Table 10's ViT-S Cars improvement is approximately 11.3 points, rather than 1.3. Section 4.4's claim of one-sixth the GradAug training cost is inconsistent with total costs of 8.6 versus 23.4 GPU-days in Table 9; that approximation concerns additional overhead, not total training cost.
